title: Indicator: EMA
description: Exponential moving average, periods 13 and 26. Foundational — consumed by MACD-Histogram, the Impulse gate, and Elder-Ray.

checklist.step: Confirm periods (13, 26) against docs/Analyse.md §4 before coding — don't invent parameters
Implement app/indicators/ema.py: pure function, DataFrame/Series in, Series out, no I/O
Write hand-computed reference-value test in tests/unit/indicators/test_ema.py (fixed small series, 2-3 asserted points, not just shape)
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: EMA is the standard recursive/iterative definition (k = 2/(period+1), EMA_t = close_t*k + EMA_{t-1}*(1-k)), seeded with the first observed value rather than an SMA warm-up average. Implemented as `series.ewm(span=period, adjust=False).mean()`.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §4 pins the periods (13, 26) but not the warm-up seeding method. Two conventions exist in the wild: (a) seed EMA_0 with the simple average of the first `period` bars, then recurse (common in charting platforms like StockCharts), or (b) seed EMA_0 with the first close and recurse from there (pandas' `ewm(adjust=False)`, and the form of the formula Elder gives directly in the book). Chose (b): it matches pandas' built-in vectorized implementation exactly (no need to hand-roll the recursion or pay for an SMA pre-roll window), it's the simpler formula to hand-verify in tests, and the two conventions converge to the same steady-state value after roughly 2-3x the period — the difference only matters in the first few bars, which this app already discards via the ~200-trading-day minimum history requirement in Analyse.md §8. Rejected SMA-seeding because Analyse.md doesn't call for it and it adds a second special-cased code path for no accuracy benefit at the data volumes this app uses.
